question.text: Per the SEBI Circular dated September 19, 2024 on modification of AIF valuation framework, which of the following is NOT a valid eligibility criterion for an independent valuer of an AIF's investment portfolio?

answer.text: IBBI-registered valuer holding ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI membership or CFA Institute charter
Holding company or subsidiary of a SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agency
A former employee of the AIF's Investment Manager who left more than 2 years ago
A Registered Valuer Entity with IBBI whose authorised person holds ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI membership or CFA charter

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pages 422-423), the independent valuer must not be an associate of the manager, sponsor or trustee, and the eligibility routes are explicitly listed: an IBBI-registered valuer with ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI membership or CFA charter, a holding company or subsidiary of a SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agency, or a Registered Valuer Entity with IBBI whose authorised person holds the same professional credentials. A former employee of the Investment Manager is not one of the listed eligibility criteria. The Trap: Options A, B and D each map to one of the three eligibility routes set out in the workbook. Option C is not on the list - independence is defined by the criteria the regulation actually states, not by a cooling-off period for former employees. Note: The eligibility list (non-associate requirement, three years of valuation experience, and the IBBI/CFA/ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI, CRA-holding/subsidiary and Registered Valuer Entity routes) is set out in pages 422-423, with cross-reference on page 510.
